Definition: from G4680; to render wise; in a sinister acceptation, to form "sophisms", i.e. continue plausible error:--cunningly devised, make wise.
BiblicalUsage: The word cuts both ways. Peter says the apostles did not follow cunningly devised fables when they made known the power and coming of the Lord, and Paul tells Timothy the holy scriptures are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the difference is everything: man's clever stories deceive, and God's Scriptures make wise.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
